findings.reason: without making the archive a place `import_ledger` reads before inserting (or excluding archived ids from the import), the sweep's effect is erased by the next promotion and the section ships a capability that does not hold.
findings.text: s12 archives rows for runs ended more than thirty days ago out of `runs` and `run_details`, but `run_store.import_ledger` walks the whole committed ledger and inserts every run "absent from the store" (reckon/run_store.py:734-784, `sync_run` inserting when `existing is None` at :351-364), and it is called on the production path by `record_gate_rerun_at_integrated_revision` (reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:1056, reached from the crew verb at reckon/crew_run_commands.py:3854); the committed ledger `ledger.load` reads is not aged by s12 — §1 places it with history-persists-as-detail-washes-out (plan.html:59-60) — so a single import pass re-inserts every archived run into the hot tables, which measured against today's store means 11,388 of 21,563 rows

findings.reason: the section names no per-pass row bound and no compaction condition, so as written the first hourly pass is an unbounded write plus a whole-file rewrite on the same pass §10 measures to five minutes, and the plan should either cap rows per pass and compact only after a pass that removed rows, or state why that cost is acceptable.
findings.text: s12 hangs an unbounded row move and a store compaction on §7's hourly `retention_sweep`, whose whole justification is that "one pass stays short on shared storage" with a fixed cap (§7 plan.html:180-183) and which §10 bounded to under five minutes; the first pass has to move 11,388 of the 21,563 rows (measured on today's store), and the store runs with `auto_vacuum=0` and `freelist_count=0`, so pages freed by the delete do not shrink the file without a full `VACUUM` that rewrites all 791,310,336 B under an exclusive lock while followers and the station page through the same file

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `~/.config/reckon/crew/run_store.db` exists at 791,310,336 B, and both cited tables resolve with 21,563 rows each (`sqlite_master` lists runs, run_details, members, holds, refusals).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — three measurable temporary-store clauses (hot-table membership, ledger and velocity fields readable through the archive, table page count falling) plus a declared negative control ("at the base revision the old run stays in the hot tables"), and `dbstat` is compiled into the store's SQLite so the page-count clause can be read (measured: runs 611,758,080 B, run_details 171,732,992 B).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the live before/after measurement now goes to the node's evidence fragment rather than the run directory §3 retires, which is the durable store §3 itself names (plan.html:118).

rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the archive is undone by an existing production caller, so the mechanism does not produce its own done-when in the real store.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable: age-based retirement of run-store rows into a separate archive file, with the compaction that follows from it.
